artists.biography:
Gomez are an English indie rock band from Southport, comprising Ian Ball (vocals, guitar), Paul "Blackie" Blackburn (bass), Tom Gray (vocals, guitars, keyboards), Ben Ottewell (vocals, guitars) and Olly Peacock (drums, synths, computers). The band is distinguished in having three singers and four songwriters, employing traditional and electronic instruments. Their sound is versatile and evades typical music genres falling into blues, indie, alternative, rock, folk, psychedelic and experimental.

Their first album, Bring It On, won the Mercury Music Prize in 1998, giving them much media attention in the UK and throughout the world. Later awards came from the NME and Q Magazine along with a Brit Awards nomination.

perplexity.description:
Liquid Skin, released in 1999 by English rock group Gomez, is the band's second studio album and a defining work in their discography. Following the success of their Mercury Prize-winning debut Bring It On, Gomez expanded their sound on Liquid Skin, blending blues rock with elements of psychedelic and alternative rock. The album features a rich tapestry of guitar textures, layered harmonies, and experimental song structures, drawing comparisons to artists like Beck, the Grateful Dead, and Pearl Jam. Recorded at Parr Street Studios in Liverpool and Abbey Road Studios in London, the band was granted creative control to self-produce, resulting in a more mature and sonically adventurous record.

Commercially, Liquid Skin was a major success, reaching number 2 on the UK Albums Chart and spawning three top 40 singles, including "Rhythm & Blues Alibi," which peaked at number 18. The album was praised for its ambitious arrangements and genre-blurring approach, solidifying Gomez’s reputation as one of the UK’s most innovative rock acts of the late 1990s. Released under Hut Records (now part of UMC/Virgin EMI Records), Liquid Skin remains a standout in Gomez’s catalog, marking a pivotal evolution in their musical style and critical acclaim.
